mutation_targets.rationale: F_AuthRequired is the sole fact that forbids a successful Operation from having no presented token. Removing it lets Alloy invent an Operation that succeeds with no auth, which the injection forces to exist; both auth predicates then find that counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthRequiredViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Success and no op.presentedToken }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_TokenBinding is the only fact pinning caller to presentedToken.owner. With it removed, the injection forces an Operation whose caller is someone other than the token owner, violating FR-002's payload-vs-context rule.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TokenBindingViolation { some op: Operation | some op.presentedToken and some op.caller and op.caller != op.presentedToken.owner }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_ClosedTaskEditRule is the sole encoder of the 409 task_closed contract. Removing it lets Alloy find a successful EditOp on a Done task whose request neither reopens it nor changes status — the injection forces exactly that shape.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskRuleViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = EditOp and op.outcome = Success and some op.target and op.target.status = Done and (no op.proposedNewStatus or op.proposedNewStatus = Done) }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_DeletionLog is the sole link between successful DeleteOps and TaskDeletion log entries. Removing it lets Alloy invent a successful delete with no corresponding log row; the injection forces that orphaned delete.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DeletionLogViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = DeleteOp and op.outcome = Success and (no td: TaskDeletion | td.fromOp = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_DeletionAttribution is the sole fact tying td.deleter to the recording op's caller. Removing it allows misattribution; the injection forces a log entry whose recorded deleter differs from the actual operation caller.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some td: TaskDeletion | td.deleter != td.fromOp.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_DeletionLogAppendOnly is the only fact that forbids two distinct TaskDeletion rows for the same delete event (duplicate / overwrite). The injection forces two log entries sharing a single source operation, which append-only must rule out.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj td1, td2: TaskDeletion | td1.fromOp = td2.fromOp }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_FlatPermissions is the only fact stating that outcome is invariant under caller identity (given same kind/target/args). Removing it lets two authenticated callers with identical requests reach different outcomes; the injection forces that role-discrimination shape.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_FlatPermissionsViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | op1.kind = op2.kind and op1.target = op2.target and op1.proposedNewStatus = op2.proposedNewStatus and some op1.caller and some op2.caller and op1.outcome != op2.outcome }
